content: Acyclovir is a medication prescribed to reduce pain and accelerate the healing of sores or blisters caused by varicella (chickenpox), herpes zoster (shingles), and genital herpes. It is also used to prevent recurrent outbreaks of genital herpes in individuals infected with the virus. Acyclovir belongs to a class of antiviral drugs known as synthetic nucleoside analogues. It works by inhibiting the replication of the herpes virus in the body. However, it does not cure genital herpes or prevent its transmission to others. Acyclovir is available in tablet, capsule, and liquid suspension forms, and it is taken orally. The medication is typically administered two to five times daily for 5 to 10 days, starting as soon as symptoms appear. For prevention of genital herpes outbreaks, it may be taken two to five times daily for up to 12 months. It is important to take the medication at the same times each day and follow the prescribed dosage exactly. Do not take more or less than directed, and do not stop taking it prematurely, even if symptoms improve, as this may result in incomplete treatment or make the infection harder to treat. If symptoms do not improve or worsen, contact your doctor. Acyclovir is also sometimes used to treat eczema herpeticum, herpes infections of the skin, eyes, nose, and mouth in individuals with HIV, and oral hairy leukoplakia. If you have questions about other potential uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting acyclovir, inform your doctor if you are allergic to acyclovir, valacyclovir, or any other medications, and provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain medications, such as amphotericin B, aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, cyclosporine, HIV medications, pentamidine, probenecid, sulfonamides, tacrolimus, and vancomycin, may interact with acyclovir. Your doctor may need to adjust dosages or monitor for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are dehydrated, have a weakened immune system, HIV, AIDS, or kidney disease, or if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you are taking acyclovir for genital herpes, be aware that the virus can still be transmitted through sexual contact, even without visible symptoms or while on medication. While taking acyclovir, it is important to stay well-hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, but if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double the dose to make up for a missed one. Acyclovir may cause side effects. Common, less severe side effects include upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, fatigue, agitation, joint pain, hair loss, and vision changes. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects requiring immediate medical attention include hives, rash, blisters, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, rapid heartbeat, weakness, pale skin, fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, blood in the urine, severe stomach pain, bloody diarrhea, decreased urination, headache, hallucinations, confusion, aggressive behavior, difficulty speaking, numbness or tingling, temporary paralysis, uncontrollable shaking, seizures, or loss of consciousness. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store acyclovir in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call emergency services at 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include agitation, seizures, extreme fatigue, loss of consciousness, swelling of the extremities, and decreased urination. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking acyclovir, as your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refills. Acyclovir is sold under the brand name Zovirax® and is also known as acycloguanosine.
